How AI for the atmosphere and ocean is changing

An interactive analysis of the catalog: which architectures, goals and data dominate, since when, what is rising or fading, what limits current models and what the papers say comes next. Every chart follows the filters, and any chart element can be clicked to slice the data.

Guided views

Each view sets up every chart below to answer one question. The filters above still apply, so you can pick a view and then narrow it to a subfield, period or architecture.

What the selection shows

    When each one arrived

    One row per category, one dot per paper (dot size = citations). The orange dot is the first paper in the catalog. Click a row name to filter; click a dot to open the paper.

    Trend by year

    The seven most common values, with the rest folded into Other. Papers with several tags count once per tag.

    Rising and fading

    Share of papers with each value before 2022 and from 2022 on.

    Rising Fading Stable (±2 pts)

    Citation impact

    Each dot is a paper: year against citations per year (log scale). The highlighted group's median is compared with the rest.

    Cross-tab explorer

    Pick any two categories and a measure. Click a cell to filter by both values. Choosing the same category for rows and columns shows co-occurrence, for example which architectures are combined.

    What the papers say is still missing

    Recurring limitations and open problems, grouped from the structured summaries. Select a theme to read what the most-cited papers in it say.

    Themes come from keyword rules over the summaries' issues and open-work fields; many of these are editorial assessments rather than the authors' own statements.

    Metadata and citation counts were retrieved from Semantic Scholar, Crossref and arXiv on . Counts differ between indexes (Google Scholar is usually higher), so use them to compare papers, not as absolute numbers. Papers with both an arXiv preprint and a published version are listed once under the published venue.
